D236179A7AFB478EB6E30687C16DD7CF.description: Support interpretations of the expressive intent and meaning of musical works citing as evidence the treatment of the elements of music, contexts, (when appropriate) the setting of the text, and varied researched sources

1D9E6824F2864933B3D2E2A44A4D49B3.description: Demonstrate mastery of the technical demands and an understanding of expressive qualities of the music in prepared and improvised performances of a varied repertoire representing diverse cultures, styles, genres, and historical periods

8CB185A7CB064E5FAB5DDADEB884FE77.description: Compose and improvise ideas for arrangements, sections, and short compositions for specific purposes that reflect characteristic(s) of music from a variety of cultures studied in rehearsal.

Identify the major components (protons, neutrons, and electrons) of the nuclear atom and explain how they interact.

Classify chemical reactions as synthesis (combination), decomposition, single displacement (replacement), double displacement, and combustion. Use stoichiometry to predict quantitative relationships in a chemical reaction.

38088710DFE70131554968A86D17958E.description: Describe the three normal states of matter in terms of energy, particle motion, and phase transitions. Describe the process of radioactive decay by using nuclear equations and explain the concept of half-life for an isotope. Compare and contrast nuclear fission and nuclear fusion.

3807F590DFE70131554768A86D17958E.description: Compare the electron configurations for the first twenty elements of the periodic table. Explain how atoms combine to form compounds through both ionic and covalent bonding. Predict chemical formulas based on the number of valence electrons. Use the mole concept to determine number of particles and molar mass for elements and compounds. Determine percent compositions, empirical formulas, and molecular formulas

38075F60DFE70131554568A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between physical properties and chemical properties. 380466B0DFE70131553B68A86D17958E.description: Use molecular models to demonstrate gene mutation and recombination at the molecular level.

38041C40DFE70131553A68A86D17958E.description: Describe the theory suggesting that life on Earth arose as a single, primitive prokaryote about 4 billion years ago and that for the next 2 billion years, a huge diversity of singlecelled organisms evolved. 37FC4C20DFE70131552168A86D17958E.description: Illustrate the formation of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids.

37FBEB60DFE70131552068A86D17958E.description: Analyze the importance of carbon to the structure of biological macromolecules. 37FB3BA0DFE70131551E68A86D17958E.description: Explain how cells differentiate in multicellular organisms.

37FAA5D0DFE70131551C68A86D17958E.description: Relate the structure of cell organelles to their function (energy capture and release, transport, waste removal, protein synthesis, movement, etc). 37FA14F0DFE70131551A68A86D17958E.description: Relate mitosis and meiosis at the molecular level.

37F78BC0DFE70131551168A86D17958E.description: Describe the common characteristics of life. document.title: Academic Standards for Reading, Writing, Speaking, and Listening (Elementary)

3AC4D1F0DFE701315B9768A86D17958E.description: Analyze the techniques of particular media messages.

3AC44610DFE701315B9568A86D17958E.description: Use media and technology resources to support personal productivity, group collaboration, and learning throughout the curriculum.

3AC36FA0DFE701315B9268A86D17958E.description: Produce an organized product that presents and reflects on findings, draws sound conclusions, and gives proper credit to sources.

3AC32240DFE701315B9168A86D17958E.description: Organization and Production of Final Product

3AC2D790DFE701315B9068A86D17958E.description: Conduct inquiry and research on self-selected or assigned topics, issues, or problems using a variety of appropriate media sources and strategies.

3AC28980DFE701315B8F68A86D17958E.description: Location of Information and Citing Sources

3AC23FC0DFE701315B8E68A86D17958E.description: Develop an inquiry based process in seeking knowledge.

3AC15A50DFE701315B8B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze differences in formal and informal language used in speech, writing, and literature.

3AC0A5B0DFE701315B8968A86D17958E.description: Characteristics and Functions of the English Language

3AC050A0DFE701315B8868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate awareness of audience using appropriate volume and clarity in formal speaking presentations.

3ABFBFE0DFE701315B8668A86D17958E.description:
Listen critically and respond to others in small and large group situations.
  • Respond with grade level appropriate questions, ideas, information, or opinions.

3ABEECD0DFE701315B8368A86D17958E.description:
Use grade appropriate conventions of language when writing and editing.
  • Spell common, frequently used words correctly.
  • Use capital letters correctly.
  • Punctuate correctly.
  • Use correct grammar and sentence formation.

3ABE49B0DFE701315B8168A86D17958E.description: Revise writing after rethinking logic of organization and rechecking central idea, content, paragraph development, level of detail, style, tone, and word choice.

3ABDB280DFE701315B7F68A86D17958E.description: Write with an understanding of style, using a variety of sentence structures and descriptive word choices. Create tone and voice through the use of precise language.

3ABD1BC0DFE701315B7D68A86D17958E.description:
Write with controlled and/or subtle organization.
  • Use appropriate transitions within sentences and between paragraphs.
  • Establish topic and purpose in the introduction.
  • Reiterate the topic and purpose in the conclusion.

3ABC8950DFE701315B7B68A86D17958E.description:
Develop content appropriate for the topic.
  • Gather, organize, and determine validity and reliability of information.
  • Employ the most effective format for purpose and audience.
  • Write paragraphs that have details and information specific to the topic and relevant to the focus.

3ABBE0E0DFE701315B7968A86D17958E.description: Write with a clear focus, identifying topic, task, and audience and establishing a single point of view.

3ABACFC0DFE701315B7668A86D17958E.description:
Write persuasive pieces.
  • Include a clearly stated position or opinion.
  • Include convincing, elaborated, and properly cited evidence.
  • Anticipate and counter reader concerns and arguments.

3ABA4EB0DFE701315B7468A86D17958E.description:
Write multi-paragraph informational pieces (e.g., letters, descriptions, reports, instructions, essays, articles, interviews).
  • Use relevant graphics (e.g. maps, charts, graphs, tables, illustrations, photographs).
  • Use primary and secondary sources, as appropriate, to task.

3AB9CB30DFE701315B7268A86D17958E.description:
Write poems, short stories, and plays.
  • Apply various organizational methods.
  • Include literary elements and devices.

3AB8DA80DFE701315B6F68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the effect of various literary devices (e.g., personification, simile, alliteration, symbolism, metaphor, hyperbole, imagery).

3AB82C60DFE701315B6D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the use of literary elements by an author including characterization, setting, plot, theme, point of view, tone, and style.

3AB7A180DFE701315B6B68A86D17958E.description: Identify and analyze the characteristics of poetry, drama, and fiction and explain the appropriateness of literary forms chosen by an author for a specific purpose.

3AB70EF0DFE701315B6968A86D17958E.description: Read, understand, and respond to works from various genres of literature.

3AB68B60DFE701315B6768A86D17958E.description: Reading, Analyzing, and Interpreting Literature - Fiction and Non-Fiction

3AB64060DFE701315B6668A86D17958E.description: Read, understand, and respond to essential content of text and documents in all academic areas.

3AB58520DFE701315B6468A86D17958E.description: Draw inferences and conclusions based on a variety of information sources, citing evidence from multiple texts to support answers.

3AB503E0DFE701315B6268A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between essential and nonessential information across a texts to a variety of media; identify bias and propaganda where present.

3AB48110DFE701315B6068A86D17958E.description: Differentiate fact from opinion utilizing resources that go beyond traditional texts (e.g., newspapers, periodicals, consumer and public documents, electronic media).

3AB3EE20DFE701315B5E68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate text organization and content to determine the author's purpose, point of view, and effectiveness according to the author's theses, accuracy, thoroughness, and patterns of logic.

3AB32D60DFE701315B5B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate an appropriate rate of silent reading based upon grade level texts.

3AB2AA00DFE701315B5968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate comprehension/understanding before reading, during reading, and after reading on grade level texts through strategies such as comparing and contrasting texts, describing context, analyzing positions and arguments, and citing evidence in text.

3AB21540DFE701315B5768A86D17958E.description: Use meaning and knowledge of words (e.g., literal and figurative meanings, idioms, common foreign words) across content areas to expand reading vocabulary.

3AB19490DFE701315B5568A86D17958E.description: Use context clues, knowledge of root words as well as a glossary/thesaurus to decode and understand specialized vocabulary in the content areas during reading.

3AB11200DFE701315B5368A86D17958E.description: Apply appropriate strategies to interpret and analyze author's purpose, using grade level text.

  • Organization: Effective organizational strategies and structures, such as logical order and transitions, to develop a position supported with a purposeful presentation of content.
  • Style: Precise control of language, stylistic techniques, and sentence structures that creates a consistent and effective tone.

3888E610DFE70131569268A86D17958E.description: Explain how the unequal heating of the Earth's surface leads to atmospheric global circulation changes, climate, local short term changes, and weather. 388849F0DFE70131569068A86D17958E.description: Explain how the ocean dominates the Earth's carbon cycle.

38879DA0DFE70131568E68A86D17958E.description: Classify Earth's internal and external sources of energy such as radioactive decay, gravity, and solar energy. Relate the transfer of energy through radiation, conduction, and convection to global atmospheric processes.

3886CF60DFE70131568C68A86D17958E.description: Describe the absolute and relative dating methods used to measure geologic time, such as index fossils, radioactive dating, law of superposition, and crosscutting relationships.

38863350DFE70131568A68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the availability, location, and extraction of Earth's resources. Evaluate the impact of using renewable and nonrenewable energy resources on the Earth's system.

38858580DFE70131568868A86D17958E.description: Explain how parts are related to other parts in weather systems, solar systems, and earth systems, including how the output from one part can become an input to another part. 76E949EAB9874E68A541810F866DA730.description: Describe the relationship between the average kinetic molecular energy, temperature, and phase changes.

932A3659B12C4A8190C1D80A73B55020.description: Analyze the factors that influence convection, conduction, and radiation between objects or regions that are at different temperatures.

0412AF4A63EA43D885ED1E0CD79BDF9C.description: Describe the law of conservation of energy. Explain the difference between an endothermic process and an exothermic process.

9315964AADFB4021ADECD930A1992580.description: Explain how energy flowing through an open system can be lost. Demonstrate how the law of conservation of momentum and conservation of energy provide alternate approaches to predict and describe the motion of objects.

387EC790DFE70131567568A86D17958E.description: Models - Recognize discoveries from Dalton (atomic theory), Thomson (the electron), Rutherford (the nucleus), and Bohr (planetary model of atom), and understand how each discovery leads to modern theory. Describe Rutherford's "gold foil" experiment that led to the discovery of the nuclear atom. Identify the major components (protons, neutrons, and electrons) of the nuclear atom and explain how they interact.

387E2340DFE70131567368A86D17958E.description: Apply oxidation/reduction principles to electrochemical reactions. Describe the interactions between acids and bases.

387DD9F0DFE70131567268A86D17958E.description: Predict how combinations of substances can result in physical and/or chemical changes. Interpret and apply the laws of conservation of mass, constant composition (definite proportions), and multiple proportions. Balance chemical equations by applying the laws of conservation of mass. Classify chemical reactions as synthesis (combination), decomposition, single displacement (replacement), double displacement, and combustion. Use stoichiometry to predict quantitative relationships in a chemical reaction.

387D48A0DFE70131567068A86D17958E.description: Explain how matter is transformed into energy in nuclear reactions according to the equation E=mc².

387CF9D0DFE70131566F68A86D17958E.description: Describe the three normal states of matter in terms of energy, particle motion, and phase transitions. Identify the three main types of radioactive decay and compare their properties. Describe the process of radioactive decay by using nuclear equations and explain the concept of half-life for an isotope. Compare and contrast nuclear fission and nuclear fusion.

387C4D40DFE70131566D68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among the isotopic forms of elements. Explain the probabilistic nature of radioactive decay based on subatomic rearrangement in the atomic nucleus. Explain how light is absorbed or emitted by electron orbital transitions.

387BFFA0DFE70131566C68A86D17958E.description: Compare the electron configurations for the first twenty elements of the periodic table. Relate the position of an element on the periodic table to its electron configuration and compare its reactivity to the reactivity of other elements in the table. Explain how atoms combine to form compounds through both ionic and covalent bonding. Predict chemical formulas based on the number of valence electrons. Draw Lewis dot structures for simple molecules and ionic compounds. Predict the chemical formulas for simple ionic and molecular compounds. Use the mole concept to determine number of particles and molar mass for elements and compounds. Determine percent compositions, empirical formulas, and molecular formulas

387B62B0DFE70131566A68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast colligative properties of mixtures. Compare and contrast the unique properties of water to other liquids.

387B0BD0DFE70131566968A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between physical properties and chemical properties. Differentiate between pure substances and mixtures; differentiate between heterogeneous and homogeneous mixtures. Explain the relationship of an element's position on the periodic table to its atomic number, ionization energy, electro-negativity, atomic size, and classification of elements. Use electro-negativity to explain the difference between polar and nonpolar covalent bonds.

38779290DFE70131565F68A86D17958E.description: Constancy and Change - Compare and contrast various theories of evolution. Interpret data from fossil records, anatomy and physiology, and DNA studies relevant to the theory of evolution. Patterns - Discuss the implications of a universal genetic code for evolution.

3876D7C0DFE70131565D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how genotypic and phenotypic variation can result in adaptations that influence an organism's success in an environment.

387687E0DFE70131565C68A86D17958E.description: Use molecular models to demonstrate gene mutation and recombination at the molecular level.

38763660DFE70131565B68A86D17958E.description: Describe the theory suggesting that life on Earth arose as a single, primitive prokaryote about 4 billion years ago and that for the next 2 billion years, a huge diversity of singlecelled organisms evolved. Analyze how increasingly complex, multicellular organisms evolved once cells with nuclei developed. Describe how mutations in sex cells may be passed on to successive generations and that the resulting phenotype may help, harm, or have little or no effect on the offspring's success in its environment. Describe the relationship between environmental changes and changes in the gene pool of a population.

38758440DFE70131565968A86D17958E.description: Analyze how natural selection leads to speciation.

38751650DFE70131565868A86D17958E.description: Describe species as reproductively distinct groups of organisms. Analyze the role that geographic isolation can play in speciation. Explain how evolution through natural selection can result in changes in biodiversity through the increase or decrease of genetic diversity within a population. Describe how the degree of kinship between species can be inferred from the similarity in their DNA sequences.

38726AB0DFE70131565068A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the societal impact of genetic engineering techniques and applications.

38721D10DFE70131564F68A86D17958E.description: Explain how genetic technologies have impacted the fields of medicine, forensics, and agriculture

38717820DFE70131564D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze gene expression at the molecular level. Explain the impact of environmental factors on gene expression.

38712A30DFE70131564C68A86D17958E.description: Describe the structure of the DNA and RNA molecules.

3870DB10DFE70131564B68A86D17958E.description: Describe the basic structure of DNA, including the role of hydrogen bonding. Explain how the process of DNA replication results in the transmission and conservation of the genetic code. Describe how transcription and translation result in gene expression. 38702CD0DFE70131564968A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the process of sexual reproduction in influencing genetic variability in a population.

Compare and contrast the function of mitosis and meiosis. Illustrate that the sorting and recombining of genes in sexual reproduction results in a great variety of possible gene combinations in offspring.

386F2820DFE70131564668A86D17958E.description: Explain gene inheritance and expression at the molecular level.

386EDAA0DFE70131564568A86D17958E.description: Explain that the information passed from parents to offspring is transmitted by means of genes which are coded in DNA molecules. Explain the basic process of DNA replication. Describe the basic processes of transcription and translation. Explain how crossing over, jumping genes, and deletion and duplication of genes results in genetic variation. Explain how mutations can alter genetic information and the possible consequences on resultant cells.

386B03B0DFE70131563A68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate metabolic activities using experimental knowledge of enzymes. Describe the potential impact of stem cell research on the biochemistry and physiology of life.

386AB2C0DFE70131563968A86D17958E.description: Illustrate the formation of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids.

386A5870DFE70131563868A86D17958E.description: Analyze the importance of carbon to the structure of biological macromolecules. 3869BFD0DFE70131563668A86D17958E.description: Analyze how cells in different tissues/organs are specialized to perform specific functions.

386975B0DFE70131563568A86D17958E.description: Explain how cells differentiate in multicellular organisms.

3868D9E0DFE70131563368A86D17958E.description: Analyze how structure is related to function at all levels of biological organization from molecules to organisms.

38686D50DFE70131563268A86D17958E.description: Relate the structure of cell organelles to their function (energy capture and release, transport, waste removal, protein synthesis, movement, etc). Explain the role of water in cell metabolism. Explain how the cell membrane functions as a regulatory structure and protective barrier for the cell. Describe transport mechanisms across the plasma membrane.

3867D640DFE70131563068A86D17958E.description: Explain how the cell cycle is regulated.

38678BC0DFE70131562F68A86D17958E.description: Relate mitosis and meiosis at the molecular level.

45839FAA0F98414084E8FE31848701B4.description:
Write informative/explanatory texts, including the narration of historical events, scientific procedures/experiments, or technical processes.
  • Introduce a topic and organize ideas, concepts, and information to make important connections and distinctions; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.
  • Develop the topic with well-chosen, relevant, and sufficient facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.
  • Use varied transitions and sentence structures to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.
  • Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to manage the complexity of the topic and convey a style appropriate to the discipline and context as well as to the expertise of likely readers.
  • Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.
  • Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

6415C60B57A94DF8882C3927B9DD9385.description:
Write arguments focused on discipline-specific content.
  • Introduce precise claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that establishes clear relationships among the claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.
  • Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly, supplying data and evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both claim(s) and counterclaims in a discipline-appropriate form and in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level and concerns.
  • Use words, phrases, and clauses to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and between claim(s) and counterclaims.
  • Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.
  • Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from or supports the argument presented.

397BA4B0DFE70131587168A86D17958E.description:
Write persuasive pieces that include a clearly stated position, convincing and properly cited evidence that anticipates and counters reader arguments and a variety of methods to advance the writer's position.
  • Focus: Sharp, distinct controlling point presented as a position and made convincing through a clear, thoughtful, and substantiated argument with evident awareness of task and audience.
  • Content: Thoroughly elaborated argument that includes a clear position consistently supported with precise and relevant evidence. Rhetorical (persuasive) strategies are evident.
  • Organization: Effective organizational strategies and structures, such as logical order and transitions, to develop a position supported with a purposeful presentation of content.
  • Style: Precise control of language, stylistic techniques, and sentence structures that creates a consistent and effective tone.
  • Conventions: Sophisticated control of grammar, mechanics, spelling, usage and sentence formation in writing.

397AB490DFE70131586E68A86D17958E.description:

  • Content: Substantial, relevant, and illustrative content that demonstrates a clear understanding of the purpose. Thorough elaboration with effectively presented information consistently supported with well-chosen details.
  • Organization: Effective organizational strategies and structures, such as logical order and transitions.
  • Style: Precise control of language, stylistic techniques, and sentence structures that creates a consistent and effective tone.

D25AFB5670624D0885E8D8E80E321B96.description:
Write informative/explanatory texts, including the narration of historical events, scientific procedures/experiments, or technical processes.
  • Introduce a topic and organize ideas, concepts, and information to make important connections and distinctions; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.
  • Develop the topic with well-chosen, relevant, and sufficient facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.
  • Use varied transitions and sentence structures to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.
  • Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to manage the complexity of the topic and convey a style appropriate to the discipline and context as well as to the expertise of likely readers.
  • Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.
  • Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

007008D769D34DCBA710B0313AF598F2.description:
Write arguments focused on discipline-specific content.
  • Introduce precise claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that establishes clear relationships among the claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.
  • Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly, supplying data and evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both claim(s) and counterclaims in a discipline-appropriate form and in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level and concerns.
  • Use words, phrases, and clauses to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and between claim(s) and counterclaims.
  • Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.
  • Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from or supports the argument presented.

  • Use data/evidence to construct explanations and understand that scientists develop explanations based on their evidence and compare them with their current scientific knowledge.

  • Punctuate correctly.

39310720DFE7013157B968A86D17958E.description: Review, evaluate, revise, edit, and proofread writing to improve style, word choice, sentence variety, and subtlety of meaning.

39305AA0DFE7013157B768A86D17958E.description: Write with an understanding of style using a variety of sentence structures and descriptive word choices. Create tone and voice through the use of precise language.

392FE090DFE7013157B668A86D17958E.description: Write with an understanding of style using precise language, action verbs, sensory details, appropriate modifiers, and the active rather than the passive voice. Create tone and voice through the use of precise language.

392F4C70DFE7013157B468A86D17958E.description:
Write with controlled and/or subtle organization.
  • Sustain a logical order throughout the piece.
  • Include an effective introduction and conclusion.

392EFF70DFE7013157B368A86D17958E.description:
Write with controlled and/or subtle organization.
  • Sustain a logical order throughout the piece.
  • Include an effective introduction and conclusion.
  • Establish coherence within and among paragraphs through effective transitions, parallel structures, and similar writing techniques.

392E6340DFE7013157B168A86D17958E.description:
Develop content appropriate for the topic.
  • Gather, organize, and determine validity and reliability of information.
  • Employ the most effective format for purpose and audience.
  • Write fully developed paragraphs that have details and information specific to the topic and relevant to the focus.

392E1B90DFE7013157B068A86D17958E.description:
Develop content appropriate for the topic.
  • Gather, organize, and determine validity and reliability of information.
  • Employ the most effective format for purpose and audience.
  • Incorporate specialized vocabulary for topic and audience
  • Write fully developed paragraphs that have details and information specific to the topic and relevant to the focus.

392D8A70DFE7013157AE68A86D17958E.description: Write with a clear focus, identifying topic, task, and audience.

392D29C0DFE7013157AD68A86D17958E.description: Write with a clear focus, identifying topic, task, and audience.

392C3450DFE7013157AA68A86D17958E.description:
Write persuasive pieces that include a clearly stated position, convincing and properly cited evidence that anticipates and counters reader arguments and a variety of methods to advance the writer's position.
  • Focus: Sharp, distinct controlling point presented as a position and made convincing through a clear, thoughtful, and substantiated argument with evident awareness of task and audience.
  • Content: Thoroughly elaborated argument that includes a clear position consistently supported with precise and relevant evidence. Rhetorical (persuasive) strategies are evident.
  • Organization: Effective organizational strategies and structures, such as logical order and transitions, to develop a position supported with a purposeful presentation of content.
  • Style: Precise control of language, stylistic techniques, and sentence structures that creates a consistent and effective tone.
  • Conventions: Sophisticated control of grammar, mechanics, spelling, usage and sentence formation in writing.

392BED50DFE7013157A968A86D17958E.description:
Write persuasive pieces.
  • Use rhetorical strategies (e.g., exposition, narration, description, argumentation, or some combination thereof) to support the main argument or position.
  • Clarify and defend positions with precise and relevant evidence, including facts, expert opinions, quotations, expressions of commonly accepted beliefs, and logical reasoning.

392BA590DFE7013157A868A86D17958E.description:
Write persuasive pieces.
  • Organize ideas and appeals in a sustained and effective fashion.
  • Use specific rhetorical devices to support assertions, such as appealing to logic through reasoning; appealing to emotion or ethical belief; or relating a personal anecdote, case study, or analogy.
  • Clarify and defend positions with precise and relevant evidence.
  • Address readers' concerns, counterclaims, biases, and expectations.

392B0400DFE7013157A668A86D17958E.description:
Write complex pieces that use precise language, employ relevant graphics, use primary/secondary sources, as appropriate and include a variety of methods to develop the main idea.
  • Focus: Sharp, distinct controlling point made about a single topic with evident awareness of task and audience.
  • Content: Substantial, relevant, and illustrative content that demonstrates a clear understanding of the purpose. Thorough elaboration with effectively presented information consistently supported with well-chosen details.
  • Organization: Effective organizational strategies and structures, such as logical order and transitions.
  • Style: Precise control of language, stylistic techniques, and sentence structures that creates a consistent and effective tone.
  • Conventions: Sophisticated control of grammar, mechanics, spelling, usage, and sentence formation in writing.

392ABD90DFE7013157A568A86D17958E.description:
Write complex informational pieces (e.g. research papers, analytical essays, summaries, descriptive pieces or literary analyses) that:
  • Gather evidence in support of a thesis.
  • Incorporate and document information and ideas from primary and secondary sources accurately and coherently.
  • Anticipate and address readers' potential misunderstandings, biases, and expectations.

392A3030DFE7013157A368A86D17958E.description:
Write poems, short stories, and plays with various organizational methods; include literary elements and devices.
  • Focus: Sharp, distinct controlling point or theme with evident awareness of the narrative.
  • Content: Strong story line with illustrative details that addresses a complex idea or examines a complex experience.
  • Organization: Skillful narrative pattern with clear and consistent sequencing of events, employing a beginning, middle, and an end.
  • Style: Precise control of language, literary devices, and sentence structures that creates a consistent and effective point of view and tone.
  • Conventions: Sophisticated control of grammar, mechanics, spelling, usage and sentence formation in writing.

3929E8C0DFE7013157A268A86D17958E.description:
Write poems, short stories, and plays.
  • Apply various organizational methods.
  • Write with an awareness of tone, mood, and elements of style.
  • Include literary elements and devices.

3928F8D0DFE70131579F68A86D17958E.description:
Interpret and analyze the author's skill in employing literary devices in various genres.
  • Identify, explain, and analyze the effect of literary devices (e.g., figurative language, imagery, allegory, and symbolism).
  • Identify, explain and analyze the effects of sound, form, and structure of poems.
  • Identify and analyze how dramatic conventions (e.g., stage directions, monologue, dialogue, soliloquy, dialect, chorus) support, interpret, and enhance dramatic script.

3928A1D0DFE70131579E68A86D17958E.description:
Evaluate the significance of various literary devices in various genre, and explain their appeal.
  • Sound (alliteration, onomatopoeia, rhyme scheme, consonance, assonance);
  • Form (ballad, sonnet, heroic couplets);
  • Figurative language personification, metaphor, simile, hyperbole, symbolism); and Dramatic structure.

3927F470DFE70131579C68A86D17958E.description:
Analyze the effectiveness of literary elements used by authors in various genres.
  • Analyze how authors develop complex characters as well as their roles and functions in a variety of texts.
  • Determine the effectiveness of setting as related to character, plot, and other key literary elements.
  • Determine the effectiveness of the author's use of point of view as related to content and specific types of genre.
  • Analyze how the author structures plot to advance the action.
  • Identify major themes in literature, comparing and contrasting how they are developed across genres.
  • Explain how voice and choice of speaker (narrator) affect the mood, tone, and meaning of text.
  • Describe how an author, through the use of diction, syntax, figurative language, sentence variety, etc., achieves style.

3927A670DFE70131579B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the use and effectiveness of literary elements (characterization, setting, plot, theme, point of view, tone, mood, foreshadowing and style) used by authors in a variety of genres.

3926FEA0DFE70131579968A86D17958E.description:
Interpret and analyze works in various genres of literary and/or cultural significance in American and world history that:
  • Reflect a variety of genres in the respective major periods of literature.
  • Represent important authors in each historical period.
  • Reveal contrasts in major themes, styles, and trends in the respective historical periods.
  • Examine the important philosophical, religious, social, political, or ethical ideas of the time.

3926BAF0DFE70131579868A86D17958E.description: Analyze the characteristics of different genres and compare works that express a universal theme and provide evidence to support the views expressed in each work.

39262F80DFE70131579668A86D17958E.description: Describe and compare the differing characteristics that distinguish the fiction and nonfiction forms of narrative, poetry, drama, and essay and determine how the form relates to meaning. Evaluate the impact of diverse cultures and writers on the development and growth of literature. Examine literature as it reflects traditional and contemporary themes, motifs, universal characters, and genres. Describe how an author conveys intent and perspective in contemporary and historical writings. Analyze the way in which a work of literature is related to the themes and issues of its historical period.

3925E980DFE70131579568A86D17958E.description: Identify the differing characteristics that distinguish the literary fiction and non-fiction forms of narrative, poetry, drama, and essay and determine how the form relates to meaning.

392505C0DFE70131579268A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure and format of various complex informational texts; Analyze and evaluate complex informational text for clarity, coherence and for the appropriateness of graphics and visual appeal.

3924B850DFE70131579168A86D17958E.description: Identify and analyze the structure and format of various informational documents and explain how authors use the features to achieve their purposes.

392329F0DFE70131578C68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between essential and nonessential information by examining an author's explicit and implicit bias and assumptions, beliefs about a subject, use of fact and/or opinion, and /or the author's argument or defense of a claim. Identify, infer, and distinguish the essential and nonessential details that support the main idea of complex texts.

3922DCC0DFE70131578B68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between essential and nonessential information across a variety of texts and sources from all academic content areas, identifying bias or propaganda where present.

39224A00DFE70131578968A86D17958E.description: Assess the accuracy of facts presented in different types of informational texts by using a variety of consumer, workplace, and public documents.

392187F0DFE70131578768A86D17958E.description: Analyze the ways in which a text's organizational structure supports or confounds its meaning or purpose.

39214560DFE70131578668A86D17958E.description: Evaluate text organization and content to determine the author's purpose and effectiveness according to the author's theses, accuracy, thoroughness, logic, and reasoning.

39207B80DFE70131578368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate an appropriate rate of silent reading based upon specific grade level texts.

391F8080DFE70131578068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate comprehension/understanding before reading, during reading, and after reading on a variety of literary works through strategies such as comparing and contrasting text elements, assessing validity of text based upon content, and evaluating author's strategies.

391EF370DFE70131577E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze textual context to determine or clarify the meaning of unfamiliar or ambiguous words and to draw conclusions about nuances or connotations of words.

391EAE00DFE70131577D68A86D17958E.description: Interpret the literal and figurative meanings of words to distinguish between what words mean literally and what they imply as well as word origins to understand both familiar and unfamiliar vocabulary.

391E1120DFE70131577B68A86D17958E.description: Use context clues, knowledge of root words, and word origins as well as reference sources to decode and understand new words.

391D86E0DFE70131577968A86D17958E.description: Apply appropriate strategies to analyze, interpret and evaluate how authors use techniques and elements of fiction and non-fiction for rhetorical and aesthetic purposes.

391D3470DFE70131577868A86D17958E.description: Apply appropriate strategies to analyze, interpret, and evaluate author's technique(s) in terms of both substance and style as related to supporting the intended purpose using grade level text.

• Distinguish between scientific fact and opinion.
  • Ask questions about objects, organisms, and events.
  • Understand that all scientific investigations involve asking and answering questions and comparing the answer with what is already known.
  • Plan and conduct a simple investigation and understand that different questions require different kinds of investigations
  • Use simple equipment (tools and other technologies) to gather data and understand that this allows scientists to collect more information than relying only on their senses to gather information.
  • Use data/evidence to construct explanations and understand that scientists develop explanations based on their evidence and compare them with their current scientific knowledge.
  • Communicate procedures and explanations giving priority to evidence and understanding that scientists make their results public, describe their investigations so they can be reproduced, and review and ask questions about the work of other scientists.

39084B5796B844B4A15DD32368428C75.description:
Write informative/explanatory texts, including the narration of historical events, scientific procedures/experiments, or technical processes.
  • Introduce a topic and organize complex ideas, concepts, and information so that each new element builds on that which precedes it to create a unified whole; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.
  • Develop the topic thoroughly by selecting the most significant and relevant facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.
  • Use varied transitions and sentence structures to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.
  • Use precise language, domain-specific vocabulary and techniques such as metaphor, simile, and analogy to manage the complexity of the topic; convey a knowledgeable stance in a style that responds to the discipline and context as well as to the expertise of likely readers.
  • Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation provided (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

F84D142CAAC64F02B25D3C5011F0ED10.description:
Write arguments focused on discipline-specific content.
  • Introduce precise, knowledgeable claim(s), establish the significance of the claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that logically sequences the claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.
  • Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly and thoroughly, supplying the most relevant data and evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both claim(s) and counterclaims in a discipline-appropriate form that anticipates the audience's knowledge level, concerns, values, and possible biases.
  • Use words, phrases, and clauses as well as varied syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and between claim(s) and counterclaims.
  • Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.
  • Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from or supports the argument presented.

26633F68039E4992AA27B068BF5184D6.description: Writing: Students write for different purposes and audiences. Students write clear and focused text to convey a well-defined perspective and appropriate content.

  • Focus: Sharp, distinct controlling point presented as a position and made convincing through a clear, thoughtful, and substantiated argument with evident awareness of task and audience.
  • Content: Thoroughly elaborated argument that includes a clear position consistently supported with precise and relevant evidence. Rhetorical (persuasive) strategies are evident.
  • Organization: Effective organizational strategies and structures, such as logical order and transitions, to develop a position supported with a purposeful presentation of content.
  • Style: Precise control of language, stylistic techniques, and sentence structures that creates a consistent and effective tone.
  • Conventions: Sophisticated control of grammar, mechanics, spelling, usage and sentence formation in writing.

39539170DFE70131580C68A86D17958E.description:

3952F890DFE70131580A68A86D17958E.description:

  • Content: Substantial, relevant, and illustrative content that demonstrates a clear understanding of the purpose. Thorough elaboration with effectively presented information consistently supported with well-chosen details.
  • Organization: Effective organizational strategies and structures, such as logical order and transitions.
  • Style: Precise control of language, stylistic techniques, and sentence structures that creates a consistent and effective tone.

2DBBEC090BE443819E8478263D69B881.description:
Write informative/explanatory texts, including the narration of historical events, scientific procedures/experiments, or technical processes.
  • Introduce a topic and organize complex ideas, concepts, and information so that each new element builds on that which precedes it to create a unified whole; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.
  • Develop the topic thoroughly by selecting the most significant and relevant facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.
  • Use varied transitions and sentence structures to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.
  • Use precise language, domain-specific vocabulary and techniques such as metaphor, simile, and analogy to manage the complexity of the topic; convey a knowledgeable stance in a style that responds to the discipline and context as well as to the expertise of likely readers.
  • Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation provided (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

BAD5B71C519842E89FE0362039D46D7E.description:
Write arguments focused on discipline-specific content.
  • Introduce precise, knowledgeable claim(s), establish the significance of the claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that logically sequences the claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.
  • Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly and thoroughly, supplying the most relevant data and evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both claim(s) and counterclaims in a discipline-appropriate form that anticipates the audience's knowledge level, concerns, values, and possible biases.
  • Use words, phrases, and clauses as well as varied syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and between claim(s) and counterclaims.
  • Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.
  • Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from or supports the argument presented.

3A0A19179EAF4930A8F9B69D6176A644.description: Describe the effects of limiting factors on population dynamics and potential species extinction.

B96C673ED0BC41228E1D737601A3B1A8.description: Describe how matter recycles through an ecosystem (i.e., water cycle, carbon cycle, oxygen cycle, and nitrogen cycle).

4C4D466133CF47CCA17CE37E4F67F221.description: Describe biotic interactions in an ecosystem (e.g., competition, predation, symbiosis).

77D927C6AC484D3B8879C464AC0352AC.description: Describe how energy flows through an ecosystem (e.g., food chains, food webs, energy pyramids).

5E6F4D47905F4012A014E703B9F25FC8.description: Describe interactions and relationships in an ecosystem.

B59EECF2CDD348C1BC09C1637502D708.description: Describe characteristic biotic and abiotic components of aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems.

12A8493AE7D844099C699A36F31F1671.description: Describe the levels of ecological organization (i.e., organism, population, community, ecosystem, biome, and biosphere).

BCCC4EB296B84BD7BB173C500C916153.description: Describe ecological levels of organization in the biosphere.

B126C4A7670F4030B278CD851862E001.description: Distinguish between the scientific terms: hypothesis, inference, law, theory, principle, fact, and observation.

11D70623C3514B51B94BB5557D3A2DE5.description: Apply scientific thinking, processes, tools, and technologies in the study of the theory of evolution.

72DBA1F5A770444C867B5B826AD51B36.description: Interpret evidence supporting the theory of evolution (i.e., fossil, anatomical, physiological, embryological, biochemical, and universal genetic code).

2244C838A4A14E2DB77555780BD6E463.description: Analyze the sources of evidence for biological evolution.

7E9975B8656D4882AF67682624D82B29.description: Explain how genetic mutations may result in genotypic and phenotypic variations within a population.

238926E49A614C668A5FED323168F6B9.description: Describe the factors that can contribute to the development of new species (e.g., isolating mechanisms, genetic drift, founder effect, migration).

7172002D0CE54B0A96255E7B49D4FCB9.description: Explain how natural selection can impact allele frequencies of a population.

3F474365058744559C4133F89ACA1E00.description: Explain how genetic engineering has impacted the fields of medicine, forensics, and agriculture (e.g., selective breeding, gene splicing, cloning, genetically modified organisms, gene therapy).

FE29AA663ACC4EC4B05B2C98A682E996.description: Apply scientific thinking, processes, tools, and technologies in the study of genetics.

01AC985D143445B7BF28A8F19B8BD1C4.description: Describe how genetic mutations alter the DNA sequence and may or may not affect phenotype (e.g., silent, nonsense, frame-shift).

91509D1D96164DDCAC29C57D3B0EF99A.description: Explain how genetic information is expressed.

876BAAA0194D4C1CAEAFB309BCF7472B.description: Describe the role of ribosomes, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, and the nucleus in the production of specific types of proteins.

BBF103560E1A4EA8BBD639634022CAF7.description: Describe how the processes of transcription and translation are similar in all organisms

AC2E10ED80DF4A11984D5D7311C5599C.description: Explain the process of protein synthesis (i.e., transcription, translation, and protein modification).

CB1439CFA1EE470EA62A81301D7E7C68.description:
Describe processes that can alter composition or number of chromosomes
(i.e., crossing-over, nondisjunction, duplication, translocation, deletion, insertion, and inversion).

3271F623F4DA408D82EB6624D98E5D13.description: Describe and/or predict observed patterns of inheritance (i.e., dominant, recessive, co-dominance, incomplete dominance, sex-linked, polygenic, and multiple alleles).

34E63BE23D2946A7A39C08978441DB62.description: Compare Mendelian and non-Mendelian patterns of inheritance.

649758F8127D45FBB81847178B18D150.description: Explain the functional relationships between DNA, genes, alleles, and chromosomes and their roles in inheritance.

82EC6DA35C7A4BF8A5594FCAE8290DE0.description: Describe how the process of DNA replication results in the transmission and/or conservation of genetic information.

D853DBDBFD7C462E9FFFA6B1CD27DCAA.description: Explain how genetic information is inherited.

3899E657F2404AE99582FB0E207C5ADC.description: Compare the processes and outcomes of mitotic and meiotic nuclear divisions.

D75F63B559994F4E9C046ADCBFD67A19.description: Describe the events that occur during the cell cycle: interphase, nuclear division (i.e., mitosis or meiosis), cytokinesis.

2A88CA0B5C9C443097C9B255187A1108.description: Describe the three stages of the cell cycle: interphase, nuclear division, cytokinesis.

4EA158CE249748E4B229F00F2E3D32E2.description: Explain how organisms maintain homeostasis (e.g., thermoregulation, water regulation, oxygen regulation).

90A5CAE275D347E898957129DFDA2B4B.description: Explain mechanisms that permit organisms to maintain biological balance between their internal and external environments.

C0C2A05A248849428637F30D9109DB5D.description: Describe how membrane-bound cellular organelles (e.g., endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus) facilitate the transport of materials within a cell.

43C8101F10DD4B8BA355CB6B046A060A.description: Compare the mechanisms that transport materials across the plasma membrane (i.e., passive transport—diffusion, osmosis, facilitated diffusion; and active transport—pumps, endocytosis, exocytosis).

50D45FDF860F444694479C33C2A9C0AC.description: Describe how the structure of the plasma membrane allows it to function as a regulatory structure and/or protective barrier for a cell.

CD0A858ECD9C4871BCEAB4E1D79D8500.description: Identify and describe the cell structures involved in transport of materials into, out of, and throughout a cell.

F0399C24CE8944679F07F7AD2A643A9B.description: Describe the role of ATP in biochemical reactions.

48D5B6C555B74A859BA83706FB585D8F.description: Compare the basic transformation of energy during photosynthesis and cellular respiration.

941B6DA27B1B48A6B4642AD7780DABD3.description: Identify and describe how organisms obtain and transform energy for their life processes.

4C56EDC806364CFB94CCAEE9B422C636.description: Describe the fundamental roles of plastids (e.g., chloroplasts) and mitochondria in energy transformations.

2C852D45A2EA46B9991A5C1F4FCFF8F5.description: Identify and describe the cell structures involved in processing energy.

81B56550E5874A838E6A384243F1FD39.description: Explain how factors such as pH, temperature, and concentration levels can affect enzyme function.

B893725E75084C0E8B2D1BE7D753FCBE.description: Describe the role of an enzyme as a catalyst in regulating a specific biochemical reaction

C8FB41A5E29843DD84E1A22E2A7BF65B.description: Explain how enzymes regulate biochemical reactions within a cell.

862DF985441C44E08A54393B41AE173C.description: Compare the structure and function of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids in organisms.

77F2A789BA194511A76C4F5739E6EEE6.description: Describe how biological macromolecules form from monomers.

5BAB1E49E4904AE3A512DF45528DBE80.description: Explain how carbon is uniquely suited to form biological macromolecules.

A9F0A7CF00FC45BF8827558810225ADA.description: Describe and interpret relationships between structure and function at various levels of biochemical organization (i.e., atoms, molecules, and macromolecules).

0600D01919B941A1926B1C33842AF472.description: Describe the unique properties of water and how these properties support life on Earth (e.g., freezing point, high specific heat, cohesion).

BFE43DA804DE46E2A7EC6FF571DB6887.description: Describe how the unique properties of water support life on Earth.

4A108EF253644FE9B0AE4C0C37D1E8EF.description: Describe and interpret relationships between structure and function at various levels of biological organization (i.e., organelles, cells, tissues, organs, organ systems, and multicellular organisms).

BBC65E36B4F34D45996EFB7CBE1D7CEF.description: Compare cellular structures and their functions in prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.

2E2B7D765D6D4C839DC68AD3D368B624.description: Describe relationships between structure and function at biological levels of organization.

BC3F73A2BF264D6C999585404587E9B4.description: Describe the characteristics of life shared by all prokaryotic and eukaryotic organisms.

B875ECF691704ADCBF9867DE7E6D9F61.description:
Explain the characteristics
common to all organisms.

Example 2: “We paid $75 for 15 hamburgers,
which is a rate of $5 per hamburger.”

7D0F5D2276754651BFD686D855CC6CF1.description:
Use ratio language and notation (such as 3 to 4,
3:4, 3/4) to describe a ratio relationship between
two quantities.
Example 1: “The ratio of girls to boys in a math
class is 2:3 because for every 2 girls there are
3 boys.”
Example 2: “For every five votes candidate A
received, candidate B received four votes.”

D7C3DD8D64864E8283B59C375538B65C.description:
Represent and/or solve real world and mathematical
problems using rates, ratios,
and/or percents.

6F02D877FD6D4974B41B2F8795452106.description: Understand ratio concepts and use ratio reasoning to solve problems

8013904A526E48EA96CAE1992AEACDD2.description:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems by
plotting points in all four quadrants of the
coordinate plane. Include use of coordinates and
absolute value to find distances between points
with the same first coordinate or the same second
coordinate.

E180A9A65D304F1991C1447C749096BB.description:
Interpret the absolute value of a rational number as
its distance from 0 on the number line and as a
magnitude for a positive or negative quantity in a
real-world situation.
Example: For an account balance of –
30 dollars,
write |–
30| = 30 to describe the size of the debt in
dollars, and recognize that an account balance
less than –
30 dollars represents a debt greater
than 30 dollars.

2E89B3B00E5E490DA2C7FD80F96D4739.description:
Write, interpret, and explain statements of order for
rational numbers in real-world contexts.
Example: Write –
3°C > –
7°C to express the fact that –
3°C is warmer than –
7°C.

3CBC1C0FD47F4C2FBF1A502F8759B2EA.description:
Understand ordering and
absolute value of rational
numbers.

322E9384B49B4B52A3504BF4AA2639F3.description:
Locate and plot integers and other rational
numbers on a horizontal or vertical number line;
locate and plot pairs of integers and other rational
numbers on a coordinate plane.

6BF39FEB59F54243B7F7E5D84AD17E66.description:
Determine the opposite of a number and recognize
that the opposite of the opposite of a number is the
number itself (e.g., –
(
–
3) = 3; 0 is its own opposite).

8716F32244314581B8850B7442E15298.description:
Represent quantities in real-world contexts using
positive and negative numbers, explaining the
meaning of 0 in each situation (e.g., temperature
above/below zero, elevation above/below sea
level, credits/debits, positive/negative electric
charge).

5E30074E4CD84E96AD1C14EB62F0C316.description:
Understand that positive and
negative numbers are used
together to describe quantities
having opposite directions or
values and locations on the
number line and coordinate
plane.

A52E1CD503474A56BC8DD78B51A38D8D.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of numbers to the system of rational numbers

FDDB0366E24149648B602ED9D4A2E203.description:
Apply the distributive property to express a sum of
two whole numbers, 1 through 100, with a common
factor as a multiple of a sum of two whole numbers
with no common factor.
Example: Express 36 + 8 as 4(9 + 2).

EE409C5FB8F94FA6BE25FC85774427FA.description:
Find the greatest common factor of two whole
numbers less than or equal to 100 and the least
common multiple of two whole numbers less than
or equal to 12.

AD0B1958AD244771A6E085CCE515927F.description:
Apply number theory concepts
(specifically, factors and
multiples).

FF096121FD0345A294C15D25441BBDF3.description:
Solve problems involving operations (+, –, ×,
and ÷) with whole numbers, decimals (through
thousandths), straight computation, or word
problems.

5C4261E292644F1A86CB1A431FC68DE6.description:
Compute with multi-digit
numbers using the four
arithmetic operations with or
without a calculator.

028FC904332B4623822AF7792A29A094.description: Compute with multi-digit numbers and find common factors and multiples

2026006F01E849E093764687629196E3.description:
Interpret and compute quotients of fractions
(including mixed numbers), and solve word
problems involving division of fractions by fractions.
Example 1: Given a story context for (2/3) ÷ (3/4),
explain that (2/3) ÷ (3/4) = 8/9 because 3/4 of 8/9 is
2/3. (In general, (a/b) ÷ (c/d) = (a/b) × (d/c) = ad/bc.)
Example 2: How wide is a rectangular strip of land
with length 3/4 mi and area 1/2 square mi?
Example 3: How many 2 1/4-foot pieces can be cut
from a 15 1/2-foot board?

FB46BA5DB20249B39E638AD03EDD4354.description:
Solve real-world and
mathematical problems involving
division of fractions.

52E2EB26A04D4BF49964EF0BE39B7AA7.description:
Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to divide fractions by
fractions.

D60A4C0556904EC4897FAA22F9C6A426.description:
Find volumes of solid figures composed of two
non-overlapping right rectangular prisms.

0E93BD444A42437A99824B1EDD29474F.description:
Apply the formulas V = l × w × h and V = B × h for
rectangular prisms to find volumes of right
rectangular prisms with whole-number edge
lengths in the context of solving real-world and
mathematical problems. Formulas will be
provided.

F26171B0F78F41F0A91D4576A78561C1.description:
Use, describe, and develop
procedures to solve problems
involving volume.

AD5071C05210477B80F3B7450F175571.description:
Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and
to addition.

1C5598E309754A5CAC089A985F4E8C8D.description:
Display and interpret data shown in tallies, tables,
charts, pictographs, bar graphs, and line graphs,
and use a title, appropriate scale, and labels. A
grid will be provided to display data on bar graphs
or line graphs.

68E81CBD89E6410F85AA8FC506C552F4.description:
Solve problems involving computation of fractions
by using information presented in line plots.

4F0AA33D1918459C845C7892A347173B.description:
Organize, display, and answer
questions based on data.

81C324FBE43E43B7AD44FB0C4288DF11.description:
Convert between different-sized measurement
units within a given measurement system. A table
of equivalencies will be provided.
Example: Convert 5 cm to meters

7E11540629844718978CDD10FE39D854.description:
Solve problems using simple
conversions (may include multistep, real-world problems).

47A530CD91794FEBA3AAAC077847A2F0.description: Convert like measurement units within a given measurement system

A38404D7EEF04A79AF7EAA385BC74D83.description:
Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy
based on properties.
Example 1: All polygons have at least three sides,
and pentagons are polygons, so all pentagons
have at least three sides.
Example 2: A rectangle is a parallelogram, which is
a quadrilateral, which is a polygon; so, a rectangle
can be classified as a parallelogram, as a
quadrilateral, and as a polygon.

C15BF830AC3E4CC8831AB39E0BD76556.description:
Use basic properties to classify
two-dimensional figures.

7BA4C792571A4BE7BA006BD6420DBEED.description: Classify two-dimensional figures into categories based on their properties.

9BB0BBDC762E48C09F829DEBE19E0EDC.description:
Represent real-world and mathematical problems
by plotting points in quadrant I of the coordinate
plane and interpret coordinate values of points in
the context of the situation.

99D37781C6F54B0683B1C94778EC097E.description:
Identify parts of the coordinate plane (x-axis, y-axis,
and the origin) and the ordered pair (x-coordinate
and y-coordinate). Limit the coordinate plane to
quadrant I.

665C200C56C04A2CAF185098694B7B41.description:
Identify parts of a coordinate
grid and describe or interpret
points given an ordered pair.

946AB365FB454D6DA79D527EF142C52F.description: Graph points on the coordinate plane to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

CDFAF8B51AC84C778E12F5F3D66FBD82.description:
Identify apparent relationships between
corresponding terms of two patterns with the same
starting numbers that follow different rules.
Example: Given two patterns in which the first
pattern follows the rule “add 8” and the second
pattern follows the rule “add 2,” observe that the
terms in the first pattern are 4 times the size of the
terms in the second pattern.

959B78698ED94CF7AA7A745864EE62C3.description:
Generate two numerical patterns using two given
rules.
Example: Given the rule “add 3” and the starting
number 0 and given the rule “add 6” and the
starting number 0, generate terms in the resulting
sequences

C169D34201AC44B8BB03960E3DB9FC25.description:
Write simple expressions that model calculations
with numbers and interpret numerical expressions
without evaluating them.
Example 1: Express the calculation “add 8 and 7,
then multiply by 2” as 2 × (8 + 7).
Example 2: Recognize that 3 × (18,932 + 921) is
three times as large as 18,932 + 921 without
having to calculate the indicated sum or product.

62D494A6C32A4074874DC83E7C191C88.description:
Use multiple grouping symbols (parentheses,
brackets, or braces) in numerical expressions and
evaluate expressions containing these symbols

E23D37F789964F689A51047836DD78FF.description:
Analyze and complete
calculations by applying the
order of operations.

00720ADBDA3946A791A4EDFB0F3FC266.description:
Divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole
numbers by unit fractions.

80FF9C498E694C6EA6448566A07D06DF.description:
Demonstrate an understanding of multiplication as
scaling (resizing).
Example 1: Comparing the size of a product to the
size of one factor on the basis of the size of the
other factor without performing the indicated
multiplication.
Example 2: Explaining why multiplying a given
number by a fraction greater than 1 results in a
product greater than the given number
(recognizing multiplication by whole numbers
greater than 1 as a familiar case); explaining why
multiplying a given number by a fraction less than
1 results in a product smaller than the given
number.

500662BF404843A784197519CBB2CDC0.description:
Multiply a fraction (including mixed numbers) by a
fraction.

EC6525F11AF54E5E92DF2307B3D5B703.description:
Solve word problems involving division of whole
numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions
(including mixed numbers).

7C4C5CFD370D4591B170F278971DDFCA.description:
Solve multiplication and division
problems involving fractions and
whole numbers (straight
computation or word problems).

BF186E1F03124F2BB50CD0C5CE94D481.description:
Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide
fractions.

82FCFE9E48894CA08E8CA987C94DF234.description:
Add and subtract fractions (including mixed
numbers) with unlike denominators. (May include
multiple methods and representations.)
Example: 2/3 + 5/4 = 8/12 + 15/12 = 23/12

3D8C859AF2E3406498E3261F4C961DD4.description:
Solve addition and subtraction
problems involving fractions
(straight computation or word
problems).

9EA4EB6104C1494DA8AAB9D21F1BC4B1.description: Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions

8BC6BA8946644A03BAA393443F229661.description:
Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to
hundredths (no divisors with decimals).

D499AF8797E5480CB378D8D8D919A941.description:
Find whole-number quotients of whole numbers
with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit
divisors.

AF4040F845134746BC37AC76A454313F.description:
Multiply multi-digit whole numbers (not to exceed
three-digit by three-digit).

40AD881D5D854048BB2F6B4575B5CD2C.description:
Use whole numbers and
decimals to compute accurately
(straight computation or word
problems).

B86BBB693C7C485B895479D2C4FF9D1B.description: Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths

0A77B3EA7F2D431588DB87614DE10BA5.description:
Round decimals to any place (limit rounding to
ones, tenths, hundredths, or thousandths place).

24B290AEBB80419EBDCB88B557EC8DA4.description:
Compare two decimals to thousandths based on
meanings of the digits in each place using >, =,
and < symbols.

EEDD3AB9BB9A4CD4B18F1169F7991C16.description:
Read and write decimals to thousandths using
base-ten numerals, word form, and expanded
form.
Example: 347.392 = 300 + 40 + 7 + 0.3 + 0.09 +
0.002 = 3 × 100 + 4 × 10

C14AC32D14484E68BD585FF1D49A4FFD.description:
Explain patterns in the number of zeros of the
product when multiplying a number by powers of
10 and explain patterns in the placement of the
decimal point when a decimal is multiplied or
divided by a power of 10. Use whole-number
exponents to denote powers of 10.
Example 1: 4 × 102 = 400
Example 2: 0.05 ÷ 103 = 0.00005

31CE4F9F370A4758B46DA058CDF2169E.description:
Demonstrate an understanding that in a multi-digit
number, a digit in one place represents 1/10 of
what it represents in the place to its left.
Example: Recognize that in the number 770, the
7 in the tens place is 1/10 the 7 in the hundreds
place.

506939311F484D3EBDA8B92B7187AD32.description:
Demonstrate understanding of
place-value of whole numbers
and decimals, and compare
quantities or magnitudes of
numbers.

58C77B767BEC4152B66B735CCF0F6733.description: Numbers and Operations in Base Ten
