document.title: PDE/SAS

FED9CC5F54884365B2A60B19E2B17CA6.description:
Find probabilities of independent compound events
using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and
simulation.

AF972D04EE654799BF213BE77AF3A962.description:
Find the probability of a simple event, including the
probability of a simple event not occurring.
Example: What is the probability of not rolling a 1
on a number cube?

4B24D728190F4B488C9C8AD393C466A6.description:
Determine the probability of a chance event given
relative frequency. Predict the approximate relative
frequency given the probability.
Example: When rolling a number cube 600 times,
predict that a 3 or 6 would be rolled roughly
200 times but probably not exactly 200 times.

033E7BF64BF14C61A45580B550A41B5B.description:
Predict or determine whether some outcomes are
certain, more likely, less likely, equally likely, or
impossible (i.e., a probability near 0 indicates an
unlikely event, a probability around 1/2 indicates an
event that is neither unlikely nor likely, and a
probability near 1 indicates a likely event).

484787A30B264AE0A4398315713C374A.description:
Predict or determine the
likelihood of outcomes.

D80A917351AB4C34BD696E5677B91544.description: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.

7F287533D11043918CD43A62E615FAD2.description:
Compare two numerical data distributions using
measures of center and variability.
Example 1: The mean height of players on the
basketball team is 10 cm greater than the mean
height of players on the soccer team. This
difference is equal to approximately twice the
variability (mean absolute deviation) on either
team. On a line plot, note the difference between
the two distributions of heights.
Example 2: Decide whether the words in a chapter
of a seventh-grade science book are generally
longer than the words in a chapter of a fourth grade science book.

A9E5B13564D147A6891597425A25DBE0.description:
Use statistical measures to
compare two numerical data
distributions.

F5FDAB562B6B48EF9FC182855A309A77.description:
Use data from a random sample to draw
inferences about a population with an unknown
characteristic of interest.
Example 1: Estimate the mean word length in a
book by randomly sampling words from the book.
Example 2: Predict the winner of a school election
based on randomly sampled survey data.

833CD2ED11E24099A3A7BD8F74D189A4.description:
Determine whether a sample is a random sample
given a real-world situation.

DAC5EAE7FF3E49838F1433B3DF1A2E0B.description: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population.

44AF8BB0BC9C42D0B799F54D6351EA27.description:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems
involving area, volume, and surface area of twoand three-dimensional objects composed of
triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, cubes, and right
prisms. Formulas will be provided.

87238AB4CA564D1E9E438BCABA84FE25.description:
Find the area and circumference of a circle. Solve
problems involving area and circumference of a
circle(s). Formulas will be provided.

4A2D4BA5D830418481067A23436712B9.description:
Determine circumference, area,
surface area, and volume.

6A4F4B76B2A4439CBEE240FB98F02334.description:
Identify and use properties of angles formed when
two parallel lines are cut by a transversal (e.g.,
angles may include alternate interior, alternate
exterior, vertical, corresponding).

B3E1490276C14B32B8492D4D900C9A66.description:
Identify and use properties of supplementary,
complementary, and adjacent angles in a multistep problem to write and solve simple equations
for an unknown angle in a figure.

D64EF61D74BC49C7964AC7F327E4EBCA.description:
Identify, use, and describe
properties of angles and their
measures.

44D3710D88854B5681021C541368530D.description:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving angle measure, circumference, area,
surface area, and volume.

3930DB0F000E4BBC966F4DD5CD9E744E.description:
Describe the two-dimensional figures that result
from slicing three-dimensional figures.
Example: Describe plane sections of right
rectangular prisms and right rectangular pyramids.

5B3315BDF53140B68B3F6C869371E88B.description: Use and apply the triangle inequality theorem.

EB5A7E9382F9488BB8C1AA348991DE09.description:
Identify or describe the properties of all types of
triangles based on angle and side measures.

E909CDD151464CA2A35D29BD9D583F8A.description:
Solve problems involving scale drawings of
geometric figures, including finding length and
area.

064812EB7980434C85C0AE355441FD3E.description:
Describe and apply properties of
geometric figures.

316AC72D8F644E58A79D1EA4BF3CDB21.description: Demonstrate an understanding of geometric figures and their properties

6247D657F45D4290A6D15CCBA9CA977C.description:
Determine the reasonableness of answer(s) or
interpret the solution(s) in the context of the
problem.
Example: If you want to place a towel bar that is
9 3/4 inches long in the center of a door that is
27 1/2 inches wide, you will need to place the
bar about 9 inches from each edge; this
estimate can be used as a check on the exact
computation.

1CB0AA8719E944E3A5199EFCA03626A0.description:
Determine the reasonableness
of the answer(s) in problem-solving situations.

99C1F3EDED704902AA9A2BAD62E9A7E3.description:
Solve word problems leading to inequalities of the
form px + q > r or px + q < r, where p, q, and r
are specific rational numbers, and graph the
solution set of the inequality.
Example: A salesperson is paid $50 per week
plus $3 per sale. This week she wants her pay to
be at least $100. Write an inequality for the
number of sales the salesperson needs to make
and describe the solutions.

61F68D2DD3CF4EE89796AC1DC2791E1E.description:
Solve word problems leading to equations of the
form px + q = r and p(x + q) = r, where p, q, and r
are specific rational numbers.
Example: The perimeter of a rectangle is 54 cm.
Its length is 6 cm. What is its width?

D47F2203ADB54AC4AB8EBD21D827F508.description:
Use variables to represent
quantities in a real-world or
mathematical problem and
construct simple equations and
inequalities to solve problems.

6896ABA19C6D496DB4B7DB66556E9386.description:
Apply properties of operations to calculate with
numbers in any form; convert between forms as
appropriate.
Example: If a woman making $25 an hour gets a
10% raise, she will make an additional 1/10 of her
salary an hour, or $2.50, for a new salary of
$27.50 an hour (or 1.1 × $25 = $27.50).

BB026667F5C14110B781293C28F4BEAB.description:
Solve multi-step real-world
and mathematical problems
posed with positive and
negative rational numbers.

FF8F6446EC2145EC802BD2180477EC0A.description:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions,
equations, and inequalities.

EB57F519C67D4A94ACE3C338D349CA32.description:
Apply properties of operations to add, subtract,
factor, and expand linear expressions with rational
coefficients.
Example 1: The expression 1/2 • (x + 6) is
equivalent to 1/2 • x + 3.
Example 2: The expression 5.3 – y + 4.2 is
equivalent to 9.5 – y (or –
y + 9.5).
Example 3: The expression 4w – 10 is equivalent
to 2(2w – 5).

74377D0048694E50A78FECDD663488E1.description:
Use properties of operations to
generate equivalent
expressions.

3BBD4F2F6B70485A87DC198542A9CDEB.description:
Use proportional relationships to solve multi-step
ratio and percent problems.
Examples: simple interest, tax, markups and
markdowns, gratuities and commissions, fees,
percent increase and decrease.

51E08C345DD2414CA0D8DD48FE5079A8.description:
Explain what a point (x, y) on the graph of a
proportional relationship means in terms of the
situation, with special attention to the points (0, 0)
and (1, r), where r is the unit rate.

76602B2DBC9D4A7C835A837D1129248A.description:
Represent proportional relationships by equations.
Example: If total cost t is proportional to the
number n of items purchased at a constant price p,
the relationship between the total cost and the
number of items can be expressed as t = pn.

F2E03FF408CE4EA89F3D87968A807539.description:
Identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in
tables, graphs, equations, diagrams, and verbal
descriptions of proportional relationships.

AD8FCBE649D14BDB9E2AF635CBD7BA16.description:
Determine whether two quantities are
proportionally related (e.g., by testing for
equivalent ratios in a table, graphing on a
coordinate plane and observing whether the graph
is a straight line through the origin).

E64C96A5317F4891A09432027471872D.description:
Compute unit rates associated with ratios of
fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas, and
other quantities measured in like or different units.
Example: If a person walks 1/2 mile in each
1/4 hour, compute the unit rate as the complex
fraction 1/2 / 1/4 miles per hour, equivalently
2 miles per hour.

738AB4F93EA348C9812401BB34857033.description:
Analyze, recognize, and
represent proportional
relationships and use them to
solve real-world and
mathematical problems.

5BF6B583BCD344A9AB04675598C49543.description: Demonstrate an understanding of proportional relationships.

031DB126D24C4C3E9815E6EAE22FB25A.description:
Apply properties of operations to multiply and
divide rational numbers, including real-world
contexts; demonstrate that the decimal form of a
rational number terminates or eventually repeats.

739061D42F194C0DB2972652DCDB83CE.description:
Represent addition and subtraction on a horizontal
or vertical number line.

70C1BCF57CCB464195E7265C05224F26.description:
Apply properties of operations to add and subtract
rational numbers, including real-world contexts.

3F8DA7E9EE3B4524BEF98D6BCDEFCBE7.description:
Solve real-world and
mathematical problems involving
the four operations with rational
numbers.

B36E81ABAA5048E0B8B9D323E4A59B1B.description:
Apply and extend previous understandings of operations to add, subtract, multiply, and divide
rational numbers.

document.title: Pennsylvania Chemistry Standards

9D776C56CFEC4681BB0C7A8DD6A73AE2.description:
Predict the amounts of reactants and products involved in a chemical reaction using molar
volume of a gas at STP.

7C8681A0CFDA490BAFE7AECFC044CEA2.description:
Utilize mathematical relationships to predict changes in the number of particles, the
temperature, the pressure, and the volume in a gaseous system (i.e., Boyle’s law,
Charles’s law, Dalton’s law of partial pressures, the combined gas law, and the ideal gas
law).

E8566CCE775745EAB6EEA297CC857740.description:
Explain how the kinetic
molecular theory relates to
the behavior of gases.

C058404372184C2F97C87400F006E71D.description: Balance chemical equations by applying the Law of Conservation of Matter.

CCC8365B44BE46BF8A01EBEBD72D67C9.description:
Predict products of simple chemical reactions (e.g., synthesis, decomposition, single
replacement, double replacement, combustion).

D31F0AED436A43B5B46CC2E788C89957.description:
3 Classify reactions as synthesis, decomposition, single replacement, double replacement,
or combustion.

E3DF299EC53F4D7DB725ABAE75303672.description:
Use stoichiometric relationships to calculate the amounts of reactants and products
involved in a chemical reaction.

AD038EDFB1A244668932C3C5E4C8ED4E.description: Describe the roles of limiting and excess reactants in chemical reactions.

DE2772872CE84496A34B0314F30358B1.description:
Predict what happens during
a chemical reaction.

550E34B305FD497590E612E12CC59DF3.description: Utilize Lewis dot structures to predict the structure and bonding in simple compounds.

DFC3291C3FF7408BBCA326E1E7C7DF16.description:
Recognize and describe different types of models that can be used to illustrate the bonds
that hold atoms together in a compound (e.g., computer models, ball‐and‐stick models,
graphical models, solid‐sphere models, structural formulas, skeletal formulas, Lewis dot
structures).

244D1EFDCA7E40AF99730A707D580310.description:
Explain how models can be
used to represent bonding.

D0104E738DA64DFE9345380203A46BAF.description: Use illustrations to predict the polarity of a molecule.

A55211ADD5BE4F4AAA6C60C92EFD5D07.description: Classify a bond as being polar covalent, non‐polar covalent, or ionic

65EF12DDAF094F07B28E30254BF53A67.description: Explain how atoms combine to form compounds through ionic and covalent bonding

80780B6E32824C6CB7AD98556DCFB645.description:
Explain how atoms form
chemical bonds.

Identify basic cloud types (i.e., cirrus,
cumulus, stratus, and cumulonimbus) and
make connections to basic elements of
weather (e.g., changes in temperature,
precipitation).

2E889C58F3B8444D85009E606F4DDB04.description:
Identify basic weather conditions and
how they are measured.
Reference: 3.5.4.C, 3.7.4.B, 3.2.4.B

5AAE5B99D9A5444EA89CC2280F0AA9BE.description:
Explain the role and relationship of a
watershed or a wetland on water sources
(e.g., water storage, groundwater
recharge, water filtration, water source,
water cycle).

0D0B2DE0A5294937B4EE94F51422F717.description:
Describe or compare lentic systems (i.e.,
ponds, lakes, and bays) and lotic systems
(i.e., streams, creeks, and rivers).

5EE7CF9A57BD437DA8B1A72ED3AD8B88.description:
Explain how water goes through phase
changes (i.e., evaporation, condensation,
freezing, and melting).

8C139832C1DC44FDAB158A3ECCEAFD0C.description:
Describe types of freshwater and
saltwater bodies (e.g., lakes, rivers,
wetlands, oceans).

6A982EC51D4C422E8FFFCD64E363D2D5.description:
Describe Earth’s different sources of
water or describe changes in the form
of water.
Reference: 3.5.4.D, 4.1.4.A, 4.1.4.D.
4.1.4.E

2039D087244A4AAFBB97A15B9921EBEB.description:
Recognize ways that humans benefit from
the use of water resources (e.g.,
agriculture, energy, recreation).

77BBD563303C4340A6BCBDA0085439A6.description:
Identify the types and uses of Earth
materials for renewable, nonrenewable,
and reusable products (e.g., human-made
products: concrete, paper, plastics,
fabrics).

09C4A05A19F14949B219EB83BE66AD03.description:
Identify products and by-products of plants
and animals for human use (e.g., food,
clothing, building materials, paper
products).

A162023A480C41BDADBA9D0D53D7AC6A.description:
Identify the types and uses of Earth’s
resources.
Reference: 3.5.4.B, 3.5.4.D, 4.2.4.B,
4.8.4.D

87AC267A344744A485CB9C058439B96B.description:
Describe the composition of soil as
weathered rock and decomposed organic
remains.

7D662D278DA54EF4883EB2046AF7C274.description:
Identify various Earth structures (e.g.,
mountains, watersheds, peninsulas,
lakes, rivers, valleys) through the use of
models.

FF28D276497A4B0E98AA2E191A300DB9.description:
Describe how prominent Earth features in
Pennsylvania (e.g., mountains, valleys,
caves, sinkholes, lakes, rivers) were
formed.

B055388354DD4D608C654E922565C9CB.description:
Describe basic landforms in
Pennsylvania.
Reference: 3.5.4.A

854A9CFD14F348279ADA0B5BFDDACED3.description: Earth Features and Processes that Change Earth and Its Resources

AB7B562A28B844A1BC0B6EFDC17F1227.description:
Describe the position of an object by
locating it relative to another object or
a stationary background (e.g.,
geographic direction, left, up).

736112052934458EA131A90966E78F82.description:
Compare the relative movement of
objects or describe types of motion
that are evident (e.g., bouncing ball,
moving in a straight line, back and
forth, merry-go-round).

2E2950A75CC744A49439A947182F1420.description:
Describe changes in motion caused
by forces (e.g., magnetic, pushes or
pulls, gravity, friction).

155E473B5A014E278BC0C5764698DBF6.description:
Identify and describe different types of
force and motion resulting from these
forces, or the effect of the interaction
between force and motion.
Reference: 3.4.4.C, 3.6.4.C, 3.2.4.B

DFA5DD3B609F43ACB9BF41A447079A5D.description:
Identify characteristics of sound (e.g.,
pitch, loudness, reflection).

EC6640FD14884C359DED68966B976B86.description:
Recognize or illustrate simple direct
current series and parallel circuits
composed of batteries, light bulbs (or
other common loads), wire, and on/off
switches.

838F527A4F9F4CE89ED4204836F430A7.description:
Describe the flow of energy through
an object or system (e.g., feeling
radiant heat from a light bulb, eating
food to get energy, using a battery to
light a bulb or run a fan).

FB10D541C63A464DB2B172AEC92ED8F0.description:
Identify energy forms, energy transfer,
and energy examples (e.g., light,
heat, electrical).

BCEAF817E5CB4BE592EE0D47504D21CD.description:
Recognize basic energy types and
sources, or describe how energy can be
changed from one form to another.
Reference: 3.4.4.B, 3.4.4.C

18FCC9A735D5481DB11D86A71725B666.description: Forms, Sources, Conversion, and Transfer of Energy

C85CD9A83AE04B8DBCABF8CB0A2627B0.description:
Use physical properties [e.g., mass,
shape, size, volume, color, texture,
magnetism, state (i.e., solid, liquid,
and gas), conductivity (i.e., electrical
and heat)] to describe matter.

0DE921AE643D4232A0EAC5947F045467.description:
Describe observable physical properties
of matter.
Reference: 3.4.4.A, 3.2.4.B

BFFEEBD24F4043CD95D6A97730AC715B.description: Structure, Properties, and Interaction of Matter and Energy

529C3BC6EB00463E8C1DCA58D36DD4AE.description:
Describe the effects of pollution (e.g.,
litter) in the community.

C316767C20FB4C1BA6F03441B495AD76.description:
Identify major land uses in the urban,
suburban and rural communities (e.g.,
housing, commercial, recreation).

6D3EBB6D47204C4EB04F871270672C6E.description:
Identify biological pests (e.g., fungi –
molds, plants – foxtail, purple
loosestrife, Eurasian water milfoil;
animals – aphides, ticks, zebra mussels,
starlings, mice) that compete with
humans for resources.

928BB5575FEA4C9599C0784C42EF9700.description:
Describe the human dependence on the
food and fiber systems from production
to consumption (e.g., food, clothing,
shelter, products).

D8098F8AD93C4BADB745BB51E7BAF24F.description:
Identify everyday human activities (e.g.,
driving, washing, eating, manufacturing,
farming) within a community that
depend on the natural environment.

03DEC0E20B8B48FC9EA116785C8DE0C5.description:
Identify and describe human reliance on
the environment at the individual or the
community level.
Reference: 4.3.4.B, 4.4.4.B, 4.5.4.C,
3.8.4.C

C8506AE8C6E84A8686731B1C22E6C54B.description:
Explain and predict how changes in
seasons affect plants, animals, or daily
human life (e.g., food availability,
shelter, mobility).

54FBFD88DA6F47EBAF12EE4F3137AEF4.description:
Describe and predict how changes in the
environment (e.g., fire, pollution, flood,
building dams) can affect systems.

1628E284E62148CC967D9407CD11954F.description:
Describe what happens to a living thing
when its habitat is changed.

701B033E6AC549CF8E360502FA92E878.description:
Describe, explain, and predict change in
natural or human-made systems and the
possible effects of those changes on the
environment.
Reference: 4.2.4.C, 4.3.4.C, 4.6.4.C

EFC59F09AF774D6896D741554A21B809.description:
Describe interactions between living and
nonliving components (e.g. plants –
water, soil, sunlight, carbon dioxide,
temperature; animals – food, water,
shelter, oxygen, temperature) of a local
ecosystem.

1201D07785714211A6686A1FC37FCA9B.description:
Describe the living and nonliving
components of a local ecosystem (e.g.,
lentic and lotic systems, forest, cornfield,
grasslands, city park, playground).

62AAEF9443344A8A9E5783DA263B877F.description:
Identify and describe living and
nonliving things in the environment and
their interaction.
Reference: 4.6.4.A

CA436FC9BE904E03A20BFE70DF916A41.description:
S4.B.2.2.1 Identify physical characteristics (e.g.,
height, hair color, eye color, attached
earlobes, ability to roll tongue) that
appear in both parents and could be
passed on to offspring.

D1D07842D81641B4917275100E7F2A16.description:
Identify that characteristics are inherited
and, thus, offspring closely resemble
their parents.
Reference: 3.3.4.C, 4.7.4.A, 4.7.4.C

E885D067B9EB4DCDA34FC803EC512CD5.description:
Explain how specific adaptations can
help a living organism survive (e.g.,
protective coloration, mimicry, leaf
sizes and shapes, ability to catch or
retain water).

D9A121743DB045B29FB6547B119ECF87.description:
Identify characteristics for plant and
animal survival in different
environments (e.g., wetland, tundra,
desert, prairie, deep ocean, forest).

29C1F0058F394290A5499B451A40A4F0.description:
Identify and explain how adaptations
help organisms to survive.
Reference: 4.7.4.B

554BD965EB20438583ECD64D12D535F7.description:
Describe the life cycles of different
organisms (e.g., moth, grasshopper,
frog, seed-producing plant).

A1C9A2D50B71437DB30734F65F6638C4.description:
Describe how different parts of a living
thing work together to provide what
the organism needs (e.g., parts of
plants: roots, stems, leaves).

42A37F581F9A4EDBB04D2032428DD8CF.description:
Describe basic needs of plants and
animals (e.g., air, water, food).

7C2254085EEB4EF8A76F71D229D79D74.description:
Compare similar functions of external
characteristics of organisms (e.g.,
anatomical characteristics:
appendages, type of covering, body
segments).

D8B2C815217A44E0AB7CBEC1AC0F756E.description:
Identify life processes of living things
(e.g., growth, digestion, respiration).

1EEBC05283FE4101A3D4ACF0F31A8D8A.description:
Identify and describe similarities and
differences between living things and
their life processes.

Reference: 3.3.4.A, 3.3.4.B, 4.3.4.A,
4.3.4.C, 4.6.4.A

347A3D364D9641609ADEBAC55D1B08F5.description:
Identify and make observations about
patterns that regularly occur and
reoccur in nature.
Reference: 3.1.4.C, 3.2.4.B

9117AB7CD38C47CD847139219893923E.description:
Use appropriate, simple modeling
tools and techniques to describe or
illustrate a system (e.g., two cans and
string to model a communications
system, terrarium to model an
ecosystem).

6010C63E968F4F68BA747D6C6B7F5FF7.description:
Use models to make observations to
explain how systems work (e.g., water
cycle, Sun-Earth-Moon system).

C29E4BE584EE430EA4462B25A8F296F2.description:
Identify what different models
represent (e.g., maps show physical
features, directions, distances; globes
represent Earth; drawings of
watersheds depict terrain; dioramas
show ecosystems; concept maps
show relationships of ideas).

A9CAA102520346B99C64C6AB2B8FEDEA.description:
Use models to illustrate simple concepts
and compare the models to what they
represent.
Reference: 3.1.4.B, 4.3.4.C

A4BDAD260EEC4EE796F2DC6B6DF601F9.description:
Identify the parts of the food and fiber
systems as they relate to agricultural
products from the source to the
consumer.

1F4A1AA3221A4F4FA4A213D97660AA8F.description:
Categorize the parts of an ecosystem
as either living or nonliving and
describe their roles in the system.

7D78544D53EB42C88250FE7BE3190923.description:
Explain a relationship between the
living and nonliving components in a
system (e.g., food web, terrarium).

802C95EE5C1A453B8813D8D3B688059E.description:
Categorize systems as either natural
or human-made (e.g., ballpoint pens,
simple electrical circuits, plant
anatomy, water cycle).

9AB1BC7F161642F196ACD356435C8324.description:
Identify systems and describe
relationships among parts of a familiar
system (e.g., digestive system, simple
machines, water cycle).
Reference: 3.1.4.A, 4.4.4.C, 4.6.4.A,
4.6.4.B, 3.6.4.A, 3.6.4.B, 3.6.4.C

2DD1EE4B6D674D0780B529028F87BAD7.description:
Identify appropriate tools or
instruments for specific tasks and
describe the information they can
provide (e.g., measuring: length -
ruler, mass - balance scale, volume -
beaker, temperature - thermometer;
making observations: hand lens,
binoculars, telescope).

506F105BE40F4380A0C372980902E3D1.description:
Identify appropriate instruments for a
specific task and describe the
information the instrument can provide.
Reference: 3.7.4.A, 3.7.4.B

6E6FF4B6AC3648E4B6CEA10111D8A909.description:
State a conclusion that is consistent
with the information/data.

08005A7BC7AF455C983F8FE6431DDCEA.description:
Observe a natural phenomenon (e.g.,
weather changes, length of
daylight/night, movement of shadows,
animal migrations, growth of plants),
record observations, and then make a
prediction based on those
observations.

F3AFB2B76B8540EFBEDD081FB1C3801A.description:
Design and describe an investigation
(a fair test) to test one variable.

AB5D13552EB04A90A05CA1EBFDEBED20.description:
Generate questions about objects,
organisms, or events that can be
answered through scientific
investigations.

99087FDD3A494A56AA2C47BAC05A854D.description:
S4.A.2.1 Apply skills necessary to conduct an
experiment or design a solution to solve
a problem

C5ECA18B6C744E19AB438DEB4E4F167E.description: Processes, Procedures, and Tools of Scientific Investigations

216F9601B326431B95E0B417953BB885.description:
Provide examples, predict, or describe
how everyday human activities (e.g.,
solid waste production, food production
and consumption, transportation, water
consumption, energy production and
use) may change the environment.

9DE3EAB0FC91415E9B7019B3C70E768E.description:
Explain what happens to a living
organism when its food supply, access
to water, shelter, or space is changed
(e.g., it might die, migrate, change
behavior, eat something else).

505BCA9A8D844158A679460C1546EECE.description:
Observe and describe the change to
objects caused by temperature change
or light.

315798D4FE484A948AF3B3FE5E7EE54A.description:
Describe relative size, distance, or
motion.

5D095C9BDFC645369B6BF970501F87A7.description:
Observe and record change by using
time and measurement.

E3FBC730A71A491591B7A330F9DB3ADA.description:
Recognize and describe change in
natural or human-made systems and
the possible effects of those changes.
Reference: 3.1.4.C, 4.7.4.B, 4.8.4.A,
4.8.4.C

8C48021530C043E5AAB8FFB9858FC9A1.description:
Identify and describe examples of
common technological changes past to
present in the community (e.g., energy
production, transportation,
communications, agriculture, packaging
materials) that have either positive or
negative impacts on society or the
environment.

011EDEC3817C47F284B443CA8C7E5763.description:
Distinguish between a scientific fact and
an opinion, providing clear explanations
that connect observations and results
(e.g., a scientific fact can be supported
by making observations).

D389AACD3C174C2893870A966FEFF537.description:
Identify and explain the application of
scientific, environmental, or
technological knowledge to possible
solutions to problems.
Reference: 3.2.4.A, 3.2.4.C, 3.8.4.C

15C7EF98E8DA4544840AB4A2E91F80B5.description:
Construct and interpret a two-way table
summarizing data on two categorical variables
collected from the same subjects. Use relative
frequencies calculated for rows or columns to
describe possible associations between the two
variables.
Example: Given data on whether students have a
curfew on school nights and whether they have
assigned chores at home, is there evidence that
those who have a curfew also tend to have
chores?

EF259906C7C54AAA8786179C9426E4F9.description:
Understand that patterns of
association can be seen in
bivariate categorical data by
displaying frequencies and
relative frequencies in a two-way
table.

C6E274F01C654C7EB1B10BB025E6E44D.description:
Use the equation of a linear model to solve
problems in the context of bivariate measurement
data, interpreting the slope and intercept.
Example: In a linear model for a biology
experiment, interpret a slope of 1.5 cm/hr as
meaning that an additional hour of sunlight each
day is associated with an additional 1.5 cm in
mature plant height.

164E018CA8EB41ECA476B3DF4ED789D3.description:
For scatter plots that suggest a linear association,
identify a line of best fit by judging the closeness of
the data points to the line.

CFC7DAF22C0C48C190AD5565967C966D.description:
Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate
measurement data to investigate patterns of
association between two quantities. Describe
patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or
negative correlation, linear association, and
nonlinear association.

832EB9B3EDAE44CBBB12F738717621B0.description:
Analyze and interpret bivariate
data displayed in multiple
representations.

F3BA0CAA0D114BCFBEB0C5280B4A4DB3.description: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.

E3BC868643FC4DDA8E1353579BAB4A5E.description:
Apply formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders,
and spheres to solve real-world and mathematical
problems. Formulas will be provided.

6102E34CAF104A528395ABACE4209949.description:
Apply volume formulas of cones,
cylinders, and spheres

85C427EBF2434D6D9F64C256CEF0088D.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume

93B95F3C0E6E4F6F8150F65681D49138.description:
Apply the Pythagorean theorem to find the
distance between two points in a coordinate
system.

6508979FE3B8436BB5F697EC7EBE35A1.description:
Apply the Pythagorean theorem to determine
unknown side lengths in right triangles in real-world
and mathematical problems in two and three
dimensions. (Figures provided for problems in
three dimensions will be consistent with Eligible
Content in grade 8 and below.)

7739C85D1375473BA5084A8C48708AB1.description:
Apply the converse of the Pythagorean theorem to
show a triangle is a right triangle.

5FAFBF8B300A45439C42ED4BCFD05CC9.description:
Solve problems involving right
triangles by applying the
Pythagorean theorem.

D387EF171225456E86B8114C2A4B7BFB.description: Understand and apply the Pythagorean theorem

0D23E24B00E448FDA0D5EC17A12DC418.description:
Given two similar two-dimensional figures,
describe a sequence of transformations that
exhibits the similarity between them.

DF5F61AF097242A98000CB7E9928BE3D.description:
Describe the effect of dilations, translations,
rotations, and reflections on two-dimensional
figures using coordinates.

43CF3218F4F2459EBC711F4FC7D4E444.description:
Given two congruent figures, describe a sequence
of transformations that exhibits the congruence
between them.

3AF2467EF60B45349A5EE0FBA8B06848.description:
Identify and apply properties of rotations,
reflections, and translations.
Example: Angle measures are preserved in
rotations, reflections, and translations.

0F6E2EE6E0F1491ABFA1E24D6A40E26F.description:
Apply properties of geometric
transformations to verify
congruence or similarity.

B3AC6FED6018433F94F22D710443E1E5.description: Demonstrate an understanding of geometric transformations.

DFE96B47609442E586483661641CF1AB.description:
Describe qualitatively the functional relationship
between two quantities by analyzing a graph (e.g.,
where the function is increasing or decreasing,
linear or nonlinear). Sketch or determine a graph
that exhibits the qualitative features of a function
that has been described verbally.

12DC2D92313C4840AABD5D726FC60D7D.description:
Construct a function to model a linear relationship
between two quantities. Determine the rate of
change and initial value of the function from a
description of a relationship or from two (x, y)
values, including reading these from a table or
from a graph. Interpret the rate of change and
initial value of a linear function in terms of the
situation it models and in terms of its graph or a
table of values.

8E293F3601A841E8BD447476C7CDA08D.description:
Represent or interpret functional
relationships between quantities
using tables, graphs, and
descriptions.

51D8A60C132A4F8397413EFE20A00A83.description: Use functions to model relationships between quantities.

4840BAAC494B46C499275975628E2986.description:
Interpret the equation y = mx + b as defining a
linear function whose graph is a straight line; give
examples of functions that are not linear.

9EE1B0C7D27149ED875019FEF627F7A5.description:
Compare properties of two functions, each
represented in a different way (i.e., algebraically,
graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal
descriptions).
Example: Given a linear function represented by a
table of values and a linear function represented by
an algebraic expression, determine which function
has the greater rate of change.

7D6D45A4F6074DEEBF364BFD879C7F22.description: Determine whether a relation is a function.

0F2C5377EAAF4BA18EA769F33CFF2130.description:
Define, evaluate, and compare
functions displayed
algebraically, graphically, or
numerically in tables or by
verbal descriptions.

E78FE588DD8148C9B102432BCB34FE68.description:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems
leading to two linear equations in two variables.
Example: Given coordinates for two pairs of points,
determine whether the line through the first pair of
points intersects the line through the second pair.

4E8BA2DD18A946CB9BE64B0AC9F69D7D.description:
Solve systems of two linear equations in two
variables algebraically and estimate solutions by
graphing the equations. Solve simple cases by
inspection.
Example: 3x + 2y = 5 and 3x + 2y = 6 have no
solution because 3x + 2y cannot simultaneously be
5 and 6.

50D3803AFD0A4086B274AA6A5251BDB6.description:
Interpret solutions to a system of two linear
equations in two variables as points of intersection
of their graphs because points of intersection
satisfy both equations simultaneously.

F39619DDC7634706889AF0E7FD8CC327.description:
Solve linear equations that have rational number
coefficients, including equations whose solutions
require expanding expressions using the
distributive property and collecting like terms.

B2238AB722E045A8BA7D30765D8F49A0.description:
Write and identify linear equations in one variable
with one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no
solutions. Show which of these possibilities is the
case by successively transforming the given
equation into simpler forms until an equivalent
equation of the form x = a, a = a, or a = b results
(where a and b are different numbers).

3440722A638D4C04917FFDC800B45FC5.description:
Write, solve, graph, and interpret
linear equations in one or two
variables, using various
methods.

5B010CD0FEC64839B9393BB201A26EF0.description: Analyze and solve linear equations and pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

41591C68D8024B8CA632C4959E3E75F9.description:
Derive the equation y = mx for a line through the
origin and the equation y = mx + b for a line
intercepting the vertical axis at b.

C9D318C8BCE94B8A8AE4A3B0E90EB3D5.description:
Use similar right triangles to show and explain why
the slope m is the same between any two distinct
points on a non-vertical line in the coordinate
plane.

C629452BAA7E426AB8C9132AF9529707.description:
Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the
unit rate as the slope of the graph. Compare two
different proportional relationships represented in
different ways.
Example: Compare a distance-time graph to a
distance-time equation to determine which of two
moving objects has greater speed.

F9706CFBDF0243BDBB5703AABE9195FF.description:
Analyze and describe linear
relationships between two
variables, using slope.

FFFB0A5E34D14F4380E32768C3F0028F.description: Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations.

1C7FE73C0DC44F96A4F8255F54AE8424.description:
Perform operations with numbers expressed in
scientific notation, including problems where both
decimal and scientific notation are used. Express
answers in scientific notation and choose units of
appropriate size for measurements of very large or
very small quantities (e.g., use millimeters per year
for seafloor spreading). Interpret scientific notation
that has been generated by technology (e.g.,
interpret 4.7EE9 displayed on a calculator as
4.7 × 109
).

A85031BF561648EC8CB34682DCF564F7.description:
Estimate very large or very small quantities by
using numbers expressed in the form of a single
digit times an integer power of 10 and express
how many times larger or smaller one number is
than another.
Example: Estimate the population of the United
States as 3 × 108 and the population of the world
as 7 × 109
 and determine that the world population
 is more than 20 times larger than the United States’
population.

B007F2D600B246D6B884F4B9F3A32490.description:
Use square root and cube root symbols to
represent solutions to equations of the form x2 = p
and x3 = p, where p is a positive rational number.
Evaluate square roots of perfect squares (up to
and including 122
) and cube roots of perfect cubes
(up to and including 53
) without a calculator.
Example: If x2 = 25 then x = ±√25.
